description: Evolve an airfoil shape optimized for maximum lift-to-drag ratio at Re=200,000 (typical drone/RC aircraft). Uses CST parameterization evaluated with XFOIL.

solution_format.description: JSON file with CST airfoil parameters

optimization_strategies.name: camber_adjustment
optimization_strategies.description: Modify difference between upper and lower coefficients to change camber
optimization_strategies.hint: More camber = higher Cl but also higher Cd. Find the sweet spot.

optimization_strategies.name: thickness_distribution
optimization_strategies.description: Adjust where maximum thickness occurs along chord
optimization_strategies.hint: Earlier max thickness = more leading edge suction. Later = lower drag.

optimization_strategies.name: leading_edge_shape
optimization_strategies.description: Tune first coefficients to modify leading edge radius
optimization_strategies.hint: Sharper LE = lower drag but earlier stall. Rounder = delayed stall.

optimization_strategies.name: trailing_edge_shape
optimization_strategies.description: Tune last coefficients for trailing edge closure
optimization_strategies.hint: Cusp vs reflexed trailing edge affects Cm and Cd.

optimization_strategies.name: symmetry_breaking
optimization_strategies.hint: Nature isn't symmetric - try unconventional combinations.

constraints: Airfoil must not self-intersect (upper above lower everywhere)
Maximum thickness must be 6-18% of chord
Maximum camber should be less than 10% of chord
Coefficients should stay within -0.4 to 0.4 range
Use 4-6 coefficients per surface (more = finer control but harder to optimize)

physics_background.reynolds_number: Re=200,000 is typical for small drones (50cm chord at 10m/s)
physics_background.lift_coefficient: Cl is dimensionless lift force. Typical cruise: 0.4-0.8
physics_background.drag_coefficient: Cd is dimensionless drag. Good airfoils: 0.005-0.020
physics_background.L_D_ratio: Lift/Drag ratio. Higher = more efficient. Target: 50-100+
physics_background.stall: At high angle of attack, flow separates and lift drops. Higher Cl_max = later stall.
